days.title: Mountains and Valleys
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Glenveagh-Tal
stops.detail: The park takes its name from the Glenveagh Valley (Gleann Bheatha, German 'Valley of Life', actually probably gleann bheithe, 'Valley of the Birch'), which splits the park into two parts.

stops.name: Derryveagh Mountains
stops.detail: It has an area of almost 16,548 hectares and is located in the Derryveagh Mountains.

stops.name: Mount Errigal
stops.detail: In its area, Mount Errigal (751 m above sea level) and Slieve Snaght (683 m above sea level) are the two highest mountains in Donegal.

stops.name: Lough Veagh
stops.detail: By the lake Lough Veagh, one finds Glenveagh Castle with its Victorian gardens and the visitor center.

stops.name: Mullangore Wood
stops.detail: The largest forest is Mullangore Wood on the southeastern shore of Lough Veagh.
